representative: Virus-level profile. Sequence length is from strain 17 (the ICTV exemplar). Whole-particle size is the ICTV family range; the capsid diameter is an HSV-1 measurement.
summary: A large enveloped DNA virus with three nested layers: an icosahedral capsid holding the genome, an irregular protein tegument around it, and a lipid envelope studded with glycoproteins. It can establish lifelong latent infection.

taxonomy.note: Formerly species Human alphaherpesvirus 1 in family Herpesviridae. The 2021 ICTV profile cited for structure predates the family's renaming to Orthoherpesviridae.

sense.note: Sense applies to single-stranded RNA genomes; a dsDNA genome has two complementary template strands.

lengthKb.note: Herpesvirus genomes span 125–241 kbp across the family (ICTV).

capsid.value: T=16 icosahedral capsid of 162 capsomers (150 hexons, 11 pentons and one portal), about 125 nm across, surrounded by a non-symmetrical tegument.

dimensions.label: Enveloped particle diameter (family range)
dimensions.note: ICTV family-level range with HSV-1 as the profile example; not an HSV-1-specific measurement.

site.value: Nucleus (transcription, genome replication, capsid packaging); maturation in the cytoplasm

mRNARoute.value: The dsDNA genome is transcribed in the nucleus in a kinetic cascade: immediate-early, then early, then late genes. Some mRNAs are spliced.

steps.title: Attachment and entry
steps.text: Envelope glycoproteins bind cell-surface receptors; entry is by membrane fusion at the cell surface or after endocytosis.

steps.title: Genome to the nucleus
steps.text: The capsid is transported to a nuclear pore and the genome enters the nucleus.

steps.title: Transcription cascade
steps.text: Immediate-early genes encode regulators, early genes the DNA replication machinery, late genes mainly virion proteins.

steps.title: Rolling-circle replication
steps.text: DNA replicates by a rolling-circle mechanism into concatemers, which are cleaved into genome lengths and packaged into preformed capsids.

steps.title: Latency (alternative outcome)
steps.text: After primary infection the virus can establish lifelong latent infection with limited gene expression.
